title: Application of Personal Law to Muslims — Section 2 Shariat Act

content.overview: Section 2 of the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937 makes Muslim Personal Law the rule of decision in the matters listed in the section, notwithstanding any custom or usage to the contrary, subject to the central Act’s agricultural-land exclusion and any State amendments.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Muslim parties? (2) Matter listed in s. 2? (3) Custom contrary — displaced? (4) Agricultural land exclusion / State amendment?
content.study:
s. 2 is the gateway that points disputes in listed fields to Muslim personal law rather than contrary custom.

Case already in migrated file: Shayara Bano v. Union of India (2017) 9 SCC 1 — personal-law practice must be analyzed by identifying legal source, statutory recognition and constitutional context; majority invalidated talaq-e-biddat for differing constitutional reasons. No additional cases invented.

sections.heading: Rule of decision
sections.body: Muslim Personal Law governs the listed matters notwithstanding contrary custom or usage.

sections.heading: Listed matters
sections.body: As enumerated in s. 2 (marriage, dissolution, maintenance, dower, gifts, succession, etc. as enacted).

sections.heading: Custom displaced
sections.body: Contrary custom or usage does not prevail in the listed field.

sections.heading: Exclusions / amendments
sections.body: Central agricultural-land exclusion and State amendments must be checked.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify matter → confirm listing → apply Muslim personal law and any special statutes (DMMA, MWA, etc.).

provisions.title: Application of personal law to Muslims

examples.title: Custom displaced
examples.body: Dispute in a listed personal-law matter — s. 2 makes Muslim personal law the rule of decision despite contrary local custom.

hypotheticals.question: Does every Muslim family dispute fall under s. 2?
hypotheticals.analysis: Only matters listed in s. 2 (and subject to exclusions/amendments). Identify the subject-matter first.

distinctions.title: s. 2 personal law vs contrary custom
distinctions.left: Muslim personal law is the rule of decision in listed matters.
distinctions.right: Custom or usage contrary to that law is displaced for those matters.

rows.right: Does not prevail in listed field.

misconceptions.trap: Custom always overrides Muslim personal law.
misconceptions.correction: In matters listed in s. 2, personal law is the rule of decision notwithstanding contrary custom.
